Incorporating Mod 2: R for Marine Science Techniqes into Plume Dissipation Workflow 
```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(patchwork)
library(here)

# Module 2 Colorblind-Safe Palette
pal_mod2 <- c(
  "Pre-Flood Baseline"  = "#0072B2",
  "Active Flood Plume"  = "#D55E00",
  "Post-Flood Recovery" = "#009E73",
  "Sensor Dropout"      = "#CC79A7"
)


# 1. Import & Clean QLD WMIP burdekin.csv (Station 120006B: Burdekin at Clare)
burdekin <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "burdekin.csv"),
  skip = 4,
  col_names = FALSE,
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  filter(str_detect(X1, "^\\d{2}:\\d{2}:\\d{2}")) %>%
  transmute(
    date             = as_date(parse_date_time(X1, orders = "HMS dmy")),
    level_m          = as.numeric(X2),
    level_qual       = as.numeric(X3),
    runoff_ML_day = as.numeric(X14),
    runoff_qual   = as.numeric(X15),
    ec_us_cm         = as.numeric(X22),
    ec_qual          = as.numeric(X23),
    water_temp_c     = as.numeric(X28)
  ) %>%
  filter(runoff_qual <= 130)


# 2. Enforce complete daily grid & flag non-random EC sensor dropouts
burdekin_ts <- burdekin %>%
  complete(date = seq.Date(min(date, na.rm = TRUE), max(date, na.rm = TRUE), by = "day")) %>%
  mutate(
    ec_status        = if_else(is.na(ec_us_cm), "Sensor Dropout (Peak Flow)", "Valid Telemetry"),
    runoff_ML_day = coalesce(runoff_ML_day, 0)
  )

# Quick check: should show 183 rows from 2023-11-01 to 2024-05-01
glimpse(burdekin_ts)


# 3. Quantify dry-season baseline (Nov-Dec 2023 Q90) & dissipation duration
baseline_q90 <- burdekin_ts %>%
  filter(month(date) %in% c(11, 12)) %>%
  summarise(q90 = quantile(runoff_ML_day, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(q90)

peak_row <- burdekin_ts %>% slice_max(runoff_ML_day, n = 1)
peak_date <- peak_row$date

recovery_date <- burdekin_ts %>%
  filter(date > peak_date, runoff_ML_day <= baseline_q90) %>%
  slice_min(date, n = 1) %>%
  pull(date)

dissipation_days <- as.numeric(recovery_date - peak_date)


# 4. Classify hydrological phases for group summaries & plotting
burdekin_phases <- burdekin_ts %>%
  mutate(
    phase = case_when(
      date < ymd("2024-01-25") ~ "Pre-Flood Baseline",
      date >= ymd("2024-01-25") & date <= recovery_date ~ "Active Flood Plume",
      TRUE ~ "Post-Flood Recovery"
    ),
    phase = factor(phase, levels = c("Pre-Flood Baseline", "Active Flood Plume", "Post-Flood Recovery"))
  )

# Summary table for your slide or Quarto report
phase_summary <- burdekin_phases %>%
  group_by(phase) %>%
  summarise(
    days = n(),
    median_runoff_ML = round(median(runoff_ML_day, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
    max_runoff_ML    = round(max(runoff_ML_day, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
    mean_temp_c         = round(mean(water_temp_c, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    ec_missing_pct      = round(mean(is.na(ec_us_cm)) * 100, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(phase_summary)

# Exporting summary table as a universal flat text file
write_csv(phase_summary,here::here("outputs/figures/floodplume_phases.csv"))

```



Using GEE Flood Plume Data 
```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(here)

# 1. Read data & clean station labels
#Extracted satellite turbidity proxy values from Google Earth Engine

gee_s3 <- read_csv(here("data", "raw", "Burdekin_S3_Plume_TimeSeries.csv")) %>%
  mutate(
    date = ymd(date),
    station = factor(station,
      levels = c("S1_Burdekin_Mouth", "S2_Magnetic_Island", "S3_Davies_Reef"),
      labels = c("Burdekin Mouth", "Magnetic Island", "Davies Reef")
    )
  )

# 2. Plot smooth trend per location
plot <- ggplot(gee_s3, aes(x = date, y = s3_turbidity_ratio, color = station, fill = station)) +
  geom_smooth(span = 0.6, linewidth = 1.3, alpha = 0.18) +
  facet_wrap(~ station) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#D55E00", "#0072B2", "#009E73"), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#D55E00", "#0072B2", "#009E73"), guide = "none") +
  labs(
    x = "Wet Season (2023 - 2024)",
    y = "Satellite Turbidity Proxy",  #Sentinel-3 from GEE
    caption = str_wrap ("Figure1. Surface Turbidity Trends Across Reef Locations. Turbidity Porxy indicates estimated level of suspended sediment and organic matter near the sea surface. Higher values indicate more suspended sediment and organic matter near the sea surface, while lower values indicate clearer oceanic water.",
  width = 120)
  ) +
theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
theme(
  plot.caption = element_text(
    size = 8,
    color = "black",
    hjust = 0,
    lineheight = 1.3,
    margin = margin(t = 15, b = 5)
  ),
  plot.caption.position = "plot",
  plot.margin = margin(
    t = 15,
    r = 20,
    b = 20,
    l = 20
  )
)

#Higher values indicate more suspended sediment and organic matter near the sea surface, while lower values indicate clearer oceanic water
print(plot)
ggsave(
  here("outputs", "figures", "FloodPlumes.png"), 
       plot, 
       width = 10, 
       height = 4, 
       dpi = 300, 
       bg = "white")

```


Using QLD Burdekin data 
```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Burdekin River Runoff & Post-Flood Dissipation Timeline (WMIP Station 120006B). Dashed green line = dry-season Q90 baseline (5,248 ML/day); shaded orange window = 81 day active flood tail" 
#| fig-width:: 12
#| fig-height:: 8

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(here)

# 1. Load & filter QLD WMIP discharge telemetry (Station 120006B: Burdekin at Clare)
burdekin_ts <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "burdekin.csv"),
  skip = 4,
  col_names = FALSE,
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  filter(str_detect(X1, "^\\d{2}:\\d{2}:\\d{2}")) %>%
  transmute(
    date             = as.Date(X1, format = "%H:%M:%S %d/%m/%Y"),
    runoff_ML_day = as.numeric(X14),
    runoff_qual   = as.numeric(X15)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(date), runoff_qual <= 130)

# 2. Compute dry-season baseline (Nov-Dec Q90), peak flow, & 81 day recovery date
baseline_q90 <- burdekin_ts %>%
  filter(month(date) %in% c(11, 12)) %>%
  summarise(q90 = quantile(runoff_ML_day, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(q90)

peak_row      <- burdekin_ts %>% slice_max(runoff_ML_day, n = 1)
peak_date     <- peak_row$date
peak_flow     <- peak_row$runoff_ML_day

recovery_date <- burdekin_ts %>%
  filter(date > peak_date, runoff_ML_day <= baseline_q90) %>%
  slice_min(date, n = 1) %>%
  pull(date)
dissipation_days <- as.numeric(recovery_date - peak_date)

# Exponential decay half-life (Peak -> Recovery)
vis_fit <- burdekin_ts %>%
  filter(date >= peak_date, date <= recovery_date) %>%
  mutate(days_since_peak = as.numeric(date - peak_date)) %>%
  lm(log(runoff_ML_day) ~ days_since_peak, data = .)

clarity <- round(-log(2) / coef(vis_fit)[["days_since_peak"]], 1) #half-life 

# 3. Build clean single-panel Figure 1 (Discharge hydrograph only)
burdekin_fp <- ggplot(burdekin_ts, aes(x = date, y = runoff_ML_day / 1000)) +
  # Shaded 81 day active flood window
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = ymd("2024-01-25"), xmax = recovery_date,
    ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
    fill = "#D55E00", alpha = 0.10
  ) +
  # Discharge area & line
  geom_area(fill = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_line(color = "#0072B2", linewidth = 1.2) +
  # Dry-season Q90 baseline dashed line
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = baseline_q90 / 1000,
    linetype = "dashed", color = "#009E73", linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  # Peak flow marker & arrow callout
  geom_point(data = peak_row, aes(x = date, y = runoff_ML_day / 1000), color = "#D55E00", size = 3) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = ymd("2023-12-08"), y = 132, hjust = 0, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold", color = "#111111",
    label = "Peak Flow: 212,272 ML/day\n(4 Feb 2024)"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "segment",
    x = ymd("2024-01-08"), y = 148, xend = peak_date - days(2), yend = (peak_flow / 1000) - 3,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")), color = "#222222", linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  # Dissipation metrics summary box in top-right
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = ymd("2024-04-29"), y = 215, hjust = 1, vjust = 1,
    size = 3.4, fontface = "bold", color = "#D55E00", fill = "white", alpha = 0.92,
    label = paste0(
      "Total Dissipation: ", dissipation_days, " days\n",
      "Flood Plume Half-Life (t½): ", clarity, " days\n",
      "Baseline Return: 25 Apr 2024"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = seq(ymd("2023-11-01"), ymd("2024-05-01"), by = "1 month"),
    date_labels = "%b"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 230)) +
  labs(
    x = "Wet Season (2023–2024)",
    y = "Riverine Runoff (1000ml/day)", 
    caption = str_wrap ("Figure2. Burdekin River Runoff & Post-Flood Dissipation Timeline (WMIP Station 120006B). The dashed green line represents baseline runoff (dry-season Q90 = 5,248 ML/day) and orange shading represnets an 81 day active flood event.",
  width = 120)                      
  ) +
theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
theme(
  plot.caption = element_text(
    size = 9,
    color = "black",
    hjust = 0,
    lineheight = 1.3,
    margin = margin(t = 15, b = 5)
  ),
  plot.caption.position = "plot",
  plot.margin = margin(
    t = 15,
    r = 20,
    b = 20,
    l = 20
  )
)

print(burdekin_fp)

ggsave(
  filename = here("outputs", "figures", "Burdekin_Runoff.png"),
  plot     = burdekin_fp,
  width    = 11,
  height   = 4.4,
  dpi      = 300,
  bg       = "white"
)

```
